title: Value tile disagrees with the same persona's brief and flow total on every housing chore, and shows no basis
expected: One figure per quantity on the topic page, with its basis (author's estimate, or measured on invented data) beside it
got: 9/9 chores show three figures for one persona: escrow $700/yr vs $4,440 brief and flow; homestead 1,200 vs 2,893; lease 900 vs 880; pmi 1,500 vs 2,732; ptax 1,100 vs 2,310; recdep 6,500 vs 15,190; s8 9,000 vs 4,970; deposit 1,500 vs 1,445; recall 700 vs 674.02. The tile says only 'for the persona'.
suggested_acceptance: Every money figure on the topic page names its basis on the same line; the Value tile and the brief total agree or the tile says how they differ

title: Rehearsal dollar figure appears only when the world was NOT shaped, yet is labelled 'shaped like your case'
expected: A rehearsal figure is either computed on a world that holds the person's facts, or labelled as the invented household's total, not as theirs
got: In 6/6 dollar rehearsals found_usd equals the bench world total exactly (880, 2,310, 15,190, 4,970, 1,445, 674.02), because dollars are kept only for renames-only worlds. Rosa's $1,445 'found' exceeds her whole $1,142.60 deduction. Marcus's recdep claimable is $2,350, not $15,190; his recall total is $600.54, not $674.02.
suggested_acceptance: A renames-only rehearsal is labelled 'the example household's figures, with your app names', never 'shaped like your case'; a dollar figure is never larger than the person's own disputed total

title: The brief has no deadlines: no date, no property, no rule named
expected: A 'Deadlines' block first: each deadline as a date, with the property and the rule (e.g. 'House: protest by 18 May, Tex. Tax Code 41.44')
got: The brief template has only lead/setup/claim/left_alone. Rosa's criterion 2 failed 8/8 and Ruth's criterion 4 failed. Deadlines appear as 'read from your papers (my guess)' or 'about 12 August 2028 (my guess)'.
suggested_acceptance: Every approved brief of a chore with a statutory or notice deadline lists it as a date, with its property and rule, before 'What I'll claim'

title: Single-state chores are offered and run out of state with nothing said
expected: The catalogue, topic and onboarding say which state's law a chore applies, and onboarding stops or adapts when the person's state differs
got: homestead and property-tax are Texas law, deposit and recdep California. 6/18 pairs ran out of state. Recdep briefs put California's 36-month rule into a Washington claim ('window ends 14 Mar 2028') and a Texas one ('about 12 August 2028'). The homestead chore ran for a Washington household, where no general homestead exemption exists.
suggested_acceptance: Each single-jurisdiction chore names its state on the catalogue row and topic page; adopting it with a person in another state yields a brief that names the governing state's rule or says the chore does not fit

title: '(my guess)' also marks the rules the playbook itself cites
expected: Three labels: 'you told me', 'the rule (source)', 'my guess'. A statute in the playbook's sources is cited, not guessed.
got: 45 guessed lines in 18 briefs. They include the RESPA one-sixth cushion and 30-day surplus (escrow M/R), Tex. Tax Code 41.44 (ptax-R), the 60-day HAP notice (s8 R/W) and Cal. Ins. 2051.5 (recdep). The slot status has only confirmed/guessed/open, and prompt rule 7 folds research into guesses. Every judge read it as 'she doesn't know the law'.
suggested_acceptance: A brief line restating a rule from economics.sources carries its source label, not '(my guess)'

title: Time-saved ratio leaves out the person's review; the review and incumbent lines are computed but never shown
expected: The ratio counts the person's review time, says it is one bench run, and shows the incumbent's fee
got: 41x for escrow becomes 17x with the 3-minute review; ptax 135x becomes 38x; recdep 103x becomes 55x. beforeAfterOf builds 'your review N min' and the incumbent line; the topic KPI renders only band.ratio.
suggested_acceptance: The Time saved tile shows review time inside the ratio (or beside it) and 'one run' when bench runs n=1

title: Topic hero tells the invented persona's story with no 'invented' label beside it; the caveat is rendered nowhere
expected: The hero brief is marked 'An example household, invented' on the same block
got: Briefs open 'A Tacoma physical therapist...' (Marcus himself), 'An Oakland teacher...', 'A Boise bookkeeper...'. The caveat is parsed and never rendered. Marcus, Rosa and Ruth read it as someone else's real case or their own.
suggested_acceptance: The topic hero shows an 'example, invented' tag and the caveat's first sentence

title: Questions locate portals but never point to a paper and line; the first card offers invented portals and leaks persona facts
expected: Questions name the paper and the line ('On the escrow letter, the line Projected tax...'); app options are open ('Which site do you use?')
got: Rosa's criterion 5 failed 7/8. 13/18 pairs corrected a portal guess. Marcus was asked about 'your husband's driver license' (he is the husband), and Ruth about 'your five apartments' (she has two houses).
suggested_acceptance: No first-round question names a playbook-world portal or a persona attribute; every question that asks for a figure names its paper and line

title: Cadence for yearly chores is 'every 365 days from today', so seasonal deadlines and one-off episodes get a nonsense schedule
expected: Yearly chores anchor to their season (property tax: early April; escrow: analysis month). Episode chores suggest no cadence.
got: suggest() turns times_per_year=1 into every_days=365 starting today+365. A property-tax chore adopted on 23 Oct first runs in Oct 2027, after the April-May window. No rule kind can anchor a date. The copy reads 'the playbook says 1 times a year'.
suggested_acceptance: Due suggests a date-anchored yearly rule for seasonal chores and none for episode chores; 'once a year' grammar

title: The cost against the consultant is never answered

got: incumbent_fee_pct exists (escrow 35, homestead 30, ptax 25, recdep 15, s8 8) and bench model cost is computed. Neither is rendered. Rosa asked in 5 pairs.
